Subject: Clarify pricing matrix + vendor form requirements

Hi Ben,

We're working through our vendor onboarding checklist and had a few questions about Redwood's usage pricing and the commit tiers you sent last week. Our procurement team noted two items they need clarified before they can sign the Preferred Vendor Form:

1) We typically expect invoices to be fixed monthly amounts tied to a PO. Your per-token usage model is fine, but procurement needs to see either (a) a minimum monthly commitment with a true-up, or (b) a guaranteed monthly invoice amount. Can you confirm if you support a baseline monthly invoice with a month-end usage reconciliation?

2) The discount schedule you provided is percent-off-per-token by cumulative monthly volume. Procurement wants the tiers expressed as committed spend bands (e.g., $100k-$250k => X% off). Would you be able to map token tiers to committed spend ranges?

3) Preferred Vendor Form: they require a PDF with a legal contact and a vendor tax id filled in. We attached our template — please confirm who on Redwood can sign and whether electronic signature (DocuSign) is acceptable.

Can you respond by EOD Monday so we can move the internal review? We have a short review window.

Thanks,
Erin Cole
Sr. Sourcing Manager
AcmeTech Procurement

Hi Erin — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front and I'll follow with a small proposal attached.

1) We can support a baseline monthly commitment with a month-end true-up. Our standard hosted offering invoices monthly; we can set a minimum committed spend and then true-up the overage at the end of each month (usage charged at the contracted per-token rate).

2) We typically publish discount tiers by tokens, but mapping to committed spend bands is straightforward once we agree on an average token cost per 1k tokens (we included a sample conversion in the attached sheet). See the attached Redwood_Pricing_Matrix_Q2_v2.xlsx — it shows three commit-strategy options: "Spend Bands (USD)", "Token Volume Tiers", and a hybrid monthly-min + overage true-up approach.

3) DocuSign is acceptable. Our legal lead typically executes the Preferred Vendor Form for commercial customers; I copied Laura and Marissa to confirm execution authority and the tax id.

Attached: Redwood_Pricing_Matrix_Q2_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Ben / Laura — quick internal note before we reply to Erin. Key procurement pushbacks I've seen across deals:

- They want an invoice/PO feel: procurement teams are uncomfortable with pure usage-open models for budgeting. Baseline monthly minimums with a clear true-up are the least-friction path.
- Spend-band discounts are easier for procurement to show in their systems (they can attach $ bands to POs).
- Preferred vendor form: legal needs our EIN and a named contract signee (doesn't have to be CEO; could be Head of Revenue or Legal).
- On tax/finance: they'll want NET30 and PO number on invoices. Our billing supports NET30; adding the PO on the invoice is standard.

I drafted two approaches in the sheet Ben attached:
A) Committed spend band (monthly) — larger discount, simpler PO workflow.
B) Token-first with monthly floor + true-up — better unit economics for variable workloads.

I recommend proposing a hybrid: a modest committed spend band (e.g., $25k/mo min for commercial) with month-end true-up and a conversion table in the SOW that maps tokens to USD for transparency. That gets procurement their PO-based invoice while preserving usage elasticity.

I'll also confirm who can sign the PreferredVendorForm_Acme.pdf; per policy legal prefers laura_bennett or our GC. Laura, can you confirm?

Marissa
Director, Partnerships Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben and Marissa — that helps. Procurement reviewed your spreadsheet and had two follow-ups:

- The $-band proposal is workable. For our internal approval matrix we need the specific bands called out (monthly committed spend ranges) and the associated effective per-token price when the band is met. The sheet had a sample but procurement asked for a final mapping so we can attach it to the PO. Can Redwood confirm the final numbers for three bands (Baseline, Mid, Scale)?

- Our finance policy requires invoices to reference a PO and be rendered as a fixed invoice amount. We can accept a monthly invoice for the committed amount plus a separate adjustment invoice for any overage true-up afterward (two-line settlement). Is Redwood able to do a committed-invoice + adjustment invoice flow (separate documents)?

- DocuSign execution is fine; legal asked that the signer be a named person with title and a tax ID included on the form. Our template also wants an insurance certificate reference — can Redwood provide a certificate of insurance (COI) at time of signature?

If you can provide a clean commit-band table and confirm the invoicing flow (committed monthly invoice + post-month true-up invoice), we can route for final sign-off. If possible, we want this in writing for our finance approvers by Wednesday COB so we can issue the PO.

Thanks — Erin

Hi Erin — appreciate the clear checklist. We can accommodate everything you've listed; propose the following final approach so procurement can onboard without delaying the go-live:

1) Commit bands (monthly committed spend / effective per-token):
   - Baseline: $25,000/month => effective price $0.00035 per token
   - Mid: $75,000/month => effective price $0.00030 per token
   - Scale: $250,000+/month => effective price $0.00024 per token
   (We will include a mapping table in the SOW that shows the assumed tokens per $ to make the conversion auditable.)

2) Invoicing flow: Redwood will issue a committed monthly invoice for the committed spend (this invoice will include the Acme PO number). At month-end we will issue a single adjustment invoice for the overage or credit, showing usage calculations and referencing the committed invoice. Two separate invoice documents is supported by our billing system. NET30 standard applies unless you need alternate terms.

3) Execution: DocuSign is fine. Redwood will sign the Preferred Vendor Form with the following signatory: Laura Bennett, VP Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference. Our tax id will be populated on the form; we'll attach a COI at signing.

4) Discount guarantee & audit: We will include a 60-day audit window in the SOW for usage reconciliation and a clause specifying that any disputes are settled via standard commercial dispute resolution (simple escalation path).

Attached: Commit_Tier_Proposal_v3.pdf (PDF summary of commit bands and sample invoices)

If this matches your requirements we'll push the Vendor Form through DocuSign and include the SOW with the detailed mapping. Erin — can you confirm the PO lead (Sanjay?) and the DocuSign recipient list so we can route correctly?
